Senses.Explanation: Literally, “not one thought arises.” The phrase is quoted in Zhang Zhuo's verse, “not a single thought arises—the whole body appears; the six faculties barely move and clouds cover it.” Yuanwu places it beside resting, not falling into sense-objects, and not dwelling in conceptual imagining. Yongjue gives an explicit explanation: “this mind functions yet is constantly still, is still yet constantly functions,” and says one's thoughts remain apart from encountered objects. The records also subject the phrase to public testing. A monk asks Yunmen whether not a single thought arising still has a fault; Yunmen answers “Mount Sumeru.” Xuedou later asks Zhimen why it has a fault and is struck when he comes forward. The headword occurs 385 times across 152 allowlisted texts.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide phrase; its affirmative use and its interrogation are different deployments of the same state, not different things.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一念不生全體現，六根纔動被雲遮
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄). Zhangzhuo Xiucai is explicitly introduced as the author of this quoted verse: the whole body appears when not one thought arises, while movement of the six faculties brings clouding. Yongjue Yuanxian quotes and comments on it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一念不生者，此心用而常寂，寂而常用，祇於自念上常離諸境
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄). Answering an unnamed questioner in his own text, Yongjue Yuanxian defines the phrase as mind functioning while still and remaining apart from encountered objects in its own thoughts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 唯是休歇到一念不生處，則便透脫，不墮情塵，不居意想
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Essentials of Chan Master Foguo Keqin (佛果克勤禪師心要). The complete instruction is Yuanwu Keqin's own direct address: Yuanwu says that resting until not one thought arises brings release from sense-dust and conceptual imagining. No embedded speaker owns the stored line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問雲門一念不生還有過也無門云須彌山
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of State Preceptor Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄), in Yulin Tongxiu's evening address. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker asking Yunmen Wenyan whether not producing a single thought still has fault; Yunmen answers Mount Sumeru. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel passage do not name the monk. The graph 門 abbreviates Yunmen here and does not name Wumen Huikai.
